Using the compact embedding for functions of bounded deformation, we prove that relaxed energy sublevels are compact without normalization on every other admissible domain, and after removing one rotational component on disks. We identify the relaxed functional with the strong formula lower semicontinuous envelope of the functional on the prescribed-trace class with integrable controlled derivatives. Then, we derive optimality conditions via convex duality. We construct explicit radial flows on annular sectors and prove that they minimize the energy over the full admissible classes, including nonradial competitors. On the square, distinct minimizers with the same prescribed boundary flux have different local collision intensities. The square--disk comparison shows that the saddle flow loses optimality when the domain changes, even after normalization.

title: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators
text: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators. For large language model (LLM) inference, prefill/decode disaggregation (P/D) is deployed in production to isolate phases with different resource demands. Attention/feed-forward network disaggregation (AFD) splits decode again, but adds communication, placement constraints, and another provisioned pool. We ask whether role-specific placement repays this cost as models and accelerator roadmaps change. Infrastructure is committed before future models and hardware can be benchmarked. We present SiliconForge, a calibrated model that varies the serving decomposition and hardware assignment independently. We compare P/D and P/D+AFD across four model directions, four accelerator classes anchored to current and announced parts, and two fabrics. We co-optimize each design using the same rules for pipeline overlap and the same power budget. Our main comparisons show no robust deployment-level AFD advantage in service-level objective (SLO) goodput per kW. Most nominal estimates favor P/D. The largest AFD lead comes from fitting one more prefill replica, not from a more efficient decode pool. AFD has a nominal lead in the KV-heavy (key-value) model direction when the co-located expert pool spans several small scale-up domains. Larger domains or a fast fabric for both designs weaken that lead. We therefore find that prefill provisioning, decode memory bandwidth, links, and pool granularity decide deployments more than the split alone. A fixed hardware assignment can lose its advantage as models, fabrics, hardware assumptions, and objectives change. Re-optimizing mappings and pool sizes on the same hardware cuts early commitment's median normalized goodput loss from 36% to 9%. We recommend adjustable mappings and pool sizes to let boundary and hardware choices follow model demands.

title: Extrapolation Matters: Sparse-Only Depth Completion Beyond LiDAR Coverage
text: Extrapolation Matters: Sparse-Only Depth Completion Beyond LiDAR Coverage. Extrapolation beyond LiDAR coverage is an important yet under-evaluated challenge of depth completion. In real camera--LiDAR systems, partial sensor overlap, occlusions, and limited field coverage often leave large image regions weakly observed or completely unobserved by LiDAR. Thus, we investigate depth completion in this beyond-coverage regime using only sparse supervision from raw single-sweep LiDAR, without dense depth labels, LiDAR accumulation, or pseudo-LiDAR generation. Our approach leverages a frozen monocular depth foundation model, lightweight per-frame alignment to sparse LiDAR geometry, and a refinement module that fuses the aligned prior with sparse LiDAR anchors to predict dense metric depth. To regularize learning under raw sparse supervision, we introduce a high-frequency normal-consistency loss defined as the image-space gradient of the per-pixel normal cosine discrepancy. This term penalizes spatial variation in scalar angular error; it does not directly match changes in neighboring normal vectors. We further introduce an evaluation protocol that explicitly separates LiDAR-supported and beyond-coverage regions, revealing extrapolative behavior that conventional depth-completion metrics can obscure. Our method achieves strong depth accuracy beyond LiDAR coverage while remaining competitive in LiDAR-covered regions, providing a practical way to deploy monocular foundation priors in multi-sensor systems.

title: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories
text: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories. Let formula be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in formula and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in formula for odd formula , in formula for formula , and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models formula for odd formula . In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.

title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
text: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction. Accurate prediction of enzyme kinetic parameters can support enzyme engineering and metabolic modeling by complementing experimental characterization. Existing prediction methods often pool residue-level protein features before combining them with substrate features. Such substrate-independent pooling cannot adapt residue weighting to the substrate during aggregation, potentially diluting information relevant to a specific enzyme-substrate pair. Since the contributions of individual residues to catalysis can depend on the substrate, substrate-conditioned aggregation offers a way to emphasize residue features relevant to the prediction. We introduce KineCouple, which uses substrate queries and residue-level keys and values in cross-attention, allowing the substrate to guide residue selection before aggregation. The model preserves the global protein representation and adds a gated correction defined as the difference between the conditioned readout and a uniform readout. ProtT5 and MolT5 remain frozen, and separate models predict kcat and Km on a logarithmic scale. In pooled out-of-fold predictions on the CataPro benchmarks, KineCouple reduces kcat RMSE from 1.333 to 1.330 and increases PCC from 0.492 to 0.496 relative to reproduced CataPro. For Km, RMSE decreases from 0.998 to 0.997 and PCC increases from 0.633 to 0.634. Spearman correlation also improves for both tasks.

title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
text: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers. Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. Rubric as Teacher uses unreachable rubrics as privileged information for reward-gated on-policy self-distillation, and Rubric as Critic decomposes saturated rubrics into child rubrics that separate current responses while sharing the parent's weight. RuACT outperforms GRPO, rubric reweighting, and rubric-guided exploration on all four medical and scientific benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and achieves the best average with Qwen3-1.7B. On initially unreachable rubrics, unguided recovery rises from 35.02% to 42.86%, while child refinement improves reward-quality alignment on independent rollouts from 57.74% to 60.77%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/RuACT.

title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
text: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms. We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power formula , consider polynomials over formula of the form formula , where formula and formula serves as an formula -linear endomorphism of formula . In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not formula , and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

title: From Prompt Engineering to Programmatic Prompting: Toward a Software Engineering Discipline for Large Language Models
text: From Prompt Engineering to Programmatic Prompting: Toward a Software Engineering Discipline for Large Language Models. The practice of instructing large language models (LLMs) through natural-language prompts has, in the span of a few years, migrated from an interactive curiosity to a load-bearing component of production software. Yet the vocabulary, tooling, and mental models of the field remain anchored in its interactive origins: we still speak of "prompt engineering" as though the crafting of a single well-worded instruction were the central problem. This paper argues for a categorical distinction. Prompt engineering, we contend, is an interaction technique - a human-computer interaction skill for eliciting desired behavior from a model in a conversational or exploratory setting. Programmatic prompting, by contrast, is an engineering discipline governing the behavioral interface between software systems and language models: the construction, composition, versioning, testing, and maintenance of prompts as first-class software artifacts embedded in larger systems. Conflating the two has produced brittle applications, unrepeatable evaluations, and an accumulation of prompt debt. We make three contributions: (1) a definition of programmatic prompting; (2) a systematic differentiation of programmatic prompting from prompt engineering, prompt tuning, fine-tuning, and general LLM application development; and (3) an account of prompt debt that distinguishes the self-admitted debt measurable in code from the silent debt that surfaces only as incidents, and identifies its economic cause. Our thesis is simple to state and consequential to accept: prompt engineering is an interaction technique; programmatic prompting is an engineering discipline.

title: Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays Derived from a U-Net Segmentation Model
text: Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays Derived from a U-Net Segmentation Model. Pneumonia killed more than 740,000 children under the age of five in 2019, and it can be difficult to recognize on chest radiographs (CXRs): opacities may be faint in early disease, may sit behind the equally bright heart shadow, and may resemble other lung conditions. Most deep learning systems treat pneumonia detection as a yes-or-no classification task. This paper asks whether a model trained on a harder task, segmenting pneumonia pixel by pixel, can be turned into an effective detector for the simpler task of deciding whether an image contains pneumonia at all. The hypothesis is that the detailed supervision of segmentation forces the network to learn where and what the disease looks like, producing a better detector than training for detection alone. A U-Net was trained to segment pneumonia on the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge dataset of 26,684 radiographs, whose rectangular bounding boxes were converted into pixel masks. The data are heavily imbalanced: 22.5% of images are positive, and only 2.6% of pixels fall inside a box, so focal loss with = 0.25 and = 2 and dropout were needed for the model to learn. On the harder segmentation task, the model reached a pixel-level F1 score of 0.45 on a held-out test set of 2,668 images. Applied to the simpler detection task, the same model reached a precision of 0.71, recall of 0.52, and F1 score of 0.60, with 91% specificity, and consistent scores on the development set. These results show that a segmentation-trained model transfers to detection while also showing where the suspected disease is. A direct comparison with a classifier trained only for detection on the same data is needed to confirm whether the segmentation-first approach is better, and is the main direction for future work.

title: Real-Time Trans-Oceanic Fiber Sensing via Convergence of Long-Reach OFDR, High-Speed Optical Networking, and RDMA-Capable Edge-GPUs
text: Real-Time Trans-Oceanic Fiber Sensing via Convergence of Long-Reach OFDR, High-Speed Optical Networking, and RDMA-Capable Edge-GPUs. We demonstrate real-time network-integrated bi-directional fiber sensing over a 4400-km subsea cable. Streaming and fusing two OFDR instruments via RDMA over a live transoceanic 130Gbaud coherent link and GPU edge-compute enabling parallel capture of multiple spatial resolutions from ~10m to ~100m.

title: Proportionality in Elections under Feasibility Constraints and Ranked Ballots: The Solid Coalition Refinement Rule
text: Proportionality in Elections under Feasibility Constraints and Ranked Ballots: The Solid Coalition Refinement Rule. We study elections with ranked ballots and general feasibility constraints, which indicate which sets of candidates are allowed as outcomes. We introduce the first proportionality axiom for this general setting and show that it extends the established notions from specific models that fit our general framework. We extend the Solid Coalition Refinement (SCR) rule to general constraints and prove that it satisfies our axiom exactly for matroid constraints. Although the naive implementation of SCR involves a step that is computationally intractable for weak orders, we show that in practical cases it can be implemented in polynomial time or efficiently in FPT time. We also illustrate limitations of this rule for approval ballots and provide its first empirical evaluation.

title: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples
text: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples. Big techs and researchers increasingly claim that their training datasets are too large to inspect for bias and ethical problems. However, in the race to build ever-large models, they have relied on automated web scraping and no human curation. Datasets built this way absorb the stereotypes, exclusionary norms, and historical prejudices of their sources, and the models trained on them can reproduce and amplify those patterns. Because manually auditing billions of samples is humanly impossible, we need practical, effective methods to identify biases in these datasets. This paper studies the feasibility of ethically auditing large datasets through small samples and proposes a practical method for identifying structural biases by applying AI Ethics Tools (AIETs) to random samples. We applied Datasheets for Datasets, Data Statements, Data Nutrition Labels, and Data Cards to a 1% sample of Framed Multi30K, and Datasheets for Datasets to two 0.00006% samples of relaion2B-en-research-safe. Our results show that evaluating small samples with AIETs can reveal ethical problems, structural biases, and technical inconsistencies. Although industry practice assumes that identifying problems requires analyzing the entire dataset, we show that a random subset supports a viable qualitative analysis without overwhelming computational or human resources. Demonstrating that a dataset is biased does not require examining every instance: if a bias appears in a random sample, it is a flaw of the creation process. The AIETs' questions acted as provocateurs, evoking different perspectives and analysis methods for the same dataset, but the analysis and its results depended fundamentally on the human factor. We hope these findings contribute to urgent public discussions about ethics, transparency, accountability, and AI regulation by offering a practical pathway for responsibly auditing massive datasets.

title: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis
text: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis. We study worst-case contagion losses in financial networks with interbank liabilities and common exposures to marketable assets. Existing linear-programming approaches provide exact stress-test values only within an insolvency-resilience margin, where all institutions remain solvent with respect to the external sector. We show that this margin is computed exactly by a finite family of linear programs, one per vertex of the uncertainty ball, whereas a single linear program based on the componentwise worst deterioration of external resources yields only a certified lower bound. We extend this framework beyond that margin in three directions. First, we derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the maximal clearing vector under arbitrary signed external net positions, providing a clearing oracle for robust stress testing when insolvency can occur. Second, we develop certified bounds on the worst-case loss beyond the margin, including insolvency-pattern enumeration, scenario lower bounds, fixed-pattern dual upper bounds, localized certificates, and a regime-generation procedure with monotone gap certificates. Third, we analyze the worst-case loss curve as a function of the perturbation radius. For formula and formula price-perturbation sets, the curve is convex, nondecreasing and piecewise linear up to the margin, with breakpoints generated by switches in worst-case shock directions, LP bases, and bank-level activity patterns. Beyond the margin, it remains nondecreasing and piecewise affine, but convexity may fail, the curve may jump upward, and the worst case need not be attained. The framework provides a certifiable MILP/LP methodology for parametric stress testing and interpretable diagnostics identifying the banks responsible for changes in systemic loss.

title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation
text: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation. Generating high-fidelity voxels while keeping their lightweight nature remains an open problem in computer vision. Current generators are either high-fidelity but computationally heavy, or lightweight but of lower fidelity. Hierarchical methods keep the lightweight nature of voxels. However, their coarse levels, which decide where all finer cells can appear, are generated with the least information about the shape and are never revisited, so they are often plausible but wrong. Our key insight is to let finer cells take part in deciding coarse cells. To this end, we propose JoVox, a discrete flow matching framework that learns the joint distribution of all levels of the voxel hierarchy, instead of a separate distribution for each level, so that coarse cells can be predicted with finer cells already generated nearby. Within this framework, we further introduce a two-level prediction, which outputs the cells two levels finer at once instead of one level finer, halving the number of levels that the network processes and yielding voxels of higher fidelity. We also introduce an unmasking strategy that revisits early decisions once finer cells are generated and corrects inconsistencies in masked diffusion models. Our framework outperforms the baselines on both unconditional and image-conditioned voxel generation. Compared with the current state-of-the-art TRELLIS.2, we achieve 8x higher training throughput, 1/15 of the FLOPs in a forward pass, train on 4 vs. 32 GPUs, and obtain higher quality with an 11% lower Chamfer distance.

title: A Geometry-Guided Feature-Space Framework for Interpretable Unsupervised 4D-STEM Analysis of Complex Multiphase Materials
text: A Geometry-Guided Feature-Space Framework for Interpretable Unsupervised 4D-STEM Analysis of Complex Multiphase Materials. Rapid, high-fidelity analysis of four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) datasets from heterogeneous materials remains challenging because coexisting phases, orientation variants, local strain gradients, and intrinsic TEM thin-foil effects produce complex, overlapping diffraction signatures. Here, we present a machine-learning (ML) framework that combines physics-informed geometric descriptors with weighted high-dimensional embeddings to identify latent structural patterns with minimal prior knowledge. By constructing a regularized descriptor space before embedding and density-based clustering, the method improves cluster stability, suppresses noise-driven fragmentation, and reduces sensitivity to embedding hyperparameters. Spatial weighting produced the largest stability gain, increasing median cluster persistence from 0.04 to 0.55 while reducing the noise fraction from approximately 22% to 0%. Rotation weighting increased DBCV from 0.80 to 0.92, although the noise fraction rose from 0.2% to 1.0%, highlighting a trade-off between improved density separation and noise rejection. We validate the framework on two benchmark systems: Si/Si formula Ge formula epitaxial layers with continuous lattice variation and deformation, and multiphase Ti-Nb alloys containing distinct phases and orientation variants. Comparisons with a pretrained vanilla autoencoder and model-free pattern vectorization show that the physics-informed geometric descriptor provides higher cluster fidelity, greater interpretability, and substantially lower dimensionality.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
text: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training. How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. Our method, Deletion Tuning, learns a binary mask over the gate projection of transformer blocks. Two practical advantages follow: the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than the corresponding FFT checkpoint, and Deletion Tuning forgets far less, which addresses a central challenge in continual learning. Under reinforcement learning, its prior-task accuracy stays near the base level while FFT, LoRA, and random sparse fine-tuning lose up to 5.4 points. To understand why masking alone suffices, we analyze the geometry of the learned weight changes under reinforcement learning using stable rank, spectrum drift, and principal-weight overlap. Compared with LoRA and random sparse fine-tuning, Deletion Tuning is closest to FFT across the three measures.

title: Causal Outcome Learning with Noisy Proxies
text: Causal Outcome Learning with Noisy Proxies. Modern observational biomedical datasets contain increasingly extensive baseline and outcome measurements, yet detecting a clinically meaningful treatment effect remains difficult because investigators must identify an outcome that captures treatment response while adjusting for confounding distributed across numerous noisy baseline variables. We introduce SCOUT (Score-based Causal Outcome Learning Using Treatment signals), a framework that learns a clinically interpretable, treatment-responsive outcome while adjusting for confounding throughout the learning process. SCOUT constructs low-dimensional adjustment representations of high-dimensional baseline measurements to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) and conditional average treatment effect (CATE) for the learned outcome. Importantly, the final adjustment space is at most two-dimensional, allowing treatment-effect heterogeneity to be estimated in this space rather than in the full high-dimensional covariate space. SCOUT also introduces a fourth-order statistic for testing treatment-effect heterogeneity that emphasizes unusually large deviations from the ATE. In synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments, the algorithm achieved competitive ATE estimation accuracy and substantially lower CATE estimation error. In an observational study of patients with bipolar disorder, SCOUT identified a clinically recognizable lithium-associated adverse-effect profile, detecting both a significant ATE (Holm-adjusted formula = 0.0026) and significant treatment-effect heterogeneity (Holm-adjusted formula = 0.033).These results demonstrate how jointly learning outcomes and controlling for confounding can facilitate the discovery of treatment effects in high-dimensional observational data.

title: Beyond Code Translation: Agentic Android-to-HarmonyOS Migration
text: Beyond Code Translation: Agentic Android-to-HarmonyOS Migration. Migrating Android applications to HarmonyOS is an important yet challenging software engineering task. Existing large language model (LLM)-based migration approaches primarily translate code at the method or file level, overlooking project-wide dependencies and workflow coordination. Moreover, ArkTS, the primary language for HarmonyOS, is relatively low-resource, and migrated applications often lack sufficient tests for reliable verification, making end-to-end migration error-prone. We present A2HTrans, an agentic framework for end-to-end Android-to-HarmonyOS application migration. Rather than performing isolated code translation, A2HTrans decomposes applications into functionality-aware migration tasks, prioritizes them through dependency analysis, and orchestrates translation, validation, and iterative repair within a unified execution workflow. To improve migration reliability, A2HTrans employs a tool-augmented verification strategy that combines compiler-based syntax checking with LLM-based semantic validation and automated repair. We evaluate A2HTrans on 14 Android applications spanning diverse sizes and domains using Claude-Sonnet-4.6 as the underlying migration model. Compared with Claude Code, A2HTrans preserves 8.3% more functional completeness, improves behavioral correctness by 8.0%, and reduces migration time by 28.8%. These results demonstrate that structured agentic execution substantially improves the reliability and efficiency of project-level cross-platform software migration.

title: MG-Cache: Multi-Granularity Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Transformer Inference
text: MG-Cache: Multi-Granularity Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Transformer Inference. Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models, while having become a powerful backbone for generative synthesis, suffer from high inference cost on generating high-resolution images. Diffusion caching has emerged as a promising acceleration technique to reduce inference cost. However, existing caching strategies fail to accurately identify the varying importance of different computational modules and rarely coordinate cache reusing across the timestep and layer granularities, making it difficult to control error accumulation. To address these limitations, we propose multi-granularity caching (MG-Cache) for DiTs, a novel and fully training-free approach to exploit computational redundancy both on timesteps and Transformer layers. Our core innovation contains a two-stage caching strategy: an offline timestep profiling analysis that identifies redundant timesteps for cache reuse, followed by an adaptive layer-wise caching strategy that combines input stability with importance of each Transformer layer to selectively cache stable Attention and MLP submodules. Extensive experiments on mainstream open-source DiT models validate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving significant acceleration while maintaining high fidelity to the uncached output, with up to a 4.18x acceleration on HunyuanVideo.

title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation
text: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation. Agentic autoregressive video generation combines semantic planning, sequential generation, and visual verification for controllable synthesis. Growing visual histories enlarge the key-value (KV) cache, increasing memory use and attention costs across candidate rollouts. Existing compression methods primarily optimize individual generators without the planner's semantic constraints, risking low priority for states supporting requested attributes or actions. We introduce SemanticKV, a training-free method for semantically aligned KV cache compression. To our knowledge, SemanticKV is the first KV cache compression method for agentic autoregressive video generation that explicitly uses planner-extracted semantic constraints to guide retention. Text cross-attention identifies constraint-related video positions, whose self-attention queries are collected into separate groups. Attention weights are averaged within each group and maximized across groups, giving each cached entry a high score when strongly used by any represented constraint. A single top-k selection retains high-scoring entries under the memory budget, leaving their keys, values, and positions unchanged. For fixed query groups and equal entry costs, this selection minimizes an additive upper bound on worst-group discarded attention. The method operates independently within each candidate without retraining or additional video generations. We evaluate four AR video backbones on three benchmarks for 5-, 30-, and 60-second generation. On Causal Forcing at a compression ratio of 0.7, SemanticKV obtains a VBench Total Score of 84.10, compared with 84.05 for the strongest compressed baseline and 83.99 for Full KV. It achieves a 1.22x speedup over Full KV and reduces KV-cache memory from 6.04 GB to 1.81 GB, a 3.35x reduction.

title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
text: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task. Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate laboratory robotics and automation with AI-driven decision-making to close the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle. However, physical testbeds that combine off-the-shelf hardware and AI into a functioning closed-loop workflow remain in early stages of development, and their integration with commercial laboratory automation is comparatively less developed. In this work, we develop a physical testbed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrate continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation. We validate this platform on a minimal closed-loop discovery task in which the system autonomously formulates aqueous dye mixtures to match a target absorbance spectrum. The system completed six independent campaigns, each consisting of 48 closed-loop iterations over approximately four hours. In every campaign, the system autonomously selected, dispensed, and measured each mixture, with an AI-driven decision-making algorithm determining subsequent formulations without human intervention. Using this testbed, we compared the performance of two AI-driven decision-making algorithms, traditional Bayesian optimization (BO) and an agentic approach, in selecting mixtures under a fixed total-volume constraint. The agentic optimizer matched target absorbance spectra using fewer iterations than BO, with reductions up to 52%, and converged on a solution for one target that BO failed to match within 48 iterations. These results demonstrate a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization, before their deployment in real-world applications where experiments may be costly and time-consuming to prepare.

title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
text: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I. We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of formula . The weighted formula - formula boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all formula , and every Schatten class between the weighted formula spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training
text: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training. Generating text-bearing images requires coherent scenes and accurate characters. Large text-to-image models improve both capabilities through repeated denoising, at substantial sampling cost. Few-step distillation reduces this cost but requires the student to organize scenes and refine glyphs within a short trajectory. We present a four-step distillation framework combining local response regularization with teacher-guided text training. Built on distribution matching, the framework distills the GLM-Image DiT while retaining its autoregressive visual prior, glyph encoder, and VAE. A path-length penalty promotes consistent local responses of the conditional denoising field. Progressive training combines synthetic strings with teacher-generated imagery to preserve character accuracy and scene-integrated typography. The student achieves GenEval Overall 0.84 and CVTG-2K word accuracy 0.5045, compared with 0.81 and 0.1690 for four-step TDM. A coefficient study favors formula , and Qwen-Image experiments show additional gains from response regularization and text supervision. Single-image inference takes 1.742 s, compared with 5.818 s for the teacher, yielding a formula speedup at the same 40 GB GPU memory requirement.

title: Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves
text: Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves. Plain weave is one of the simplest woven structures, formed by two sets of yarns that cross at right angles in an alternating over-under pattern. While such woven fabrics are usually confined to a 2D surface, here we propose a practical approach to fabricate volumetric plain weaves, entanglements featuring three mutually orthogonal families of yarns threaded through a cubic lattice. We develop an analytic framework that converts the crossing pattern topology into continuous yarn centreline geometries, which we then leverage to fabricate volumetric weave specimens. Each crossing is encoded by a matrix that defines the offsets of the three yarns at a vertex. These are formulated to preserve the plain weave topology in every plane, where each pair of yarn families interlaces as in a planar plain weave. Eight configurations in four opposite pairs exist, yet all are related by rotations and translations, so that the fully alternating volumetric plain weave has a single topology. We adopt sinusoidal yarn trajectories and show that the crossing matrix defines their phases. We select two solutions: in-phase planar zigzags and out-of-phase circular helices. Both are members of a family of elliptical helices that also admits a free choice of handedness for each yarn. We then derive the conditions under which yarns intersect between vertices. In-phase yarns never intersect, whereas helical yarns of equal handedness intersect at a critical offset of formula , with formula the wavelength of the cubic lattice. No assignment of handedness avoids these intersections. Finally, we fabricate volumetric plain weaves by 3D printing and manual assembly from cotton cord. The framework provides a direct basis for generating weave geometries for simulation and fabrication.

title: Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching
text: Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching. We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a Kahler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact Kahler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least formula is biholomorphic to formula , formula , or the first Hirzebruch surface formula . For pinching strictly greater than formula , only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on formula and formula .

title: Co-Creating Neurorehabilitation Technology Alongside Lived Experience Experts: A Participatory Design Workshop
text: Co-Creating Neurorehabilitation Technology Alongside Lived Experience Experts: A Participatory Design Workshop. Involving patients' lived experience (LE) early in neurorehabilitation technology design can improve the relevance and effectiveness of solutions, yet LE experts are often involved only when finished prototypes are tested. We present and evaluate a participatory design (PD) workshop for early LE involvement, examine how LE contributions influence design processes and outcomes, and provide recommendations for similar approaches. We conducted a PD workshop at the 6th International Conference on NeuroRehabilitation. Five people who have had a stroke (LE experts) and 18 workshop attendees (including the LE experts' caregivers) were organized into five groups. Following the Discover, Define, and Develop phases of the Double Diamond model, each group used Journey Maps and Data Collection Notebooks to co-create a solution for an objective specified by an LE expert. Journey Maps were thematically analyzed, and group audio transcripts underwent structured extraction using a large language model. LE input shifted discussions from discipline-based assumptions toward priorities grounded in lived experience, including fear, confidence, sensory discomfort, fatigue, aesthetics, and independence. Narrow objectives, such as opening a blister pack, produced task-specific solutions, whereas broader objectives generated device concepts, including sensory feedback for cycling and a stimulation-equipped cooking splint. Satisfaction was high among attendees and LE experts. All workshop tools and protocols are shared to support adoption. The workshop offers a practical foundation for involving LE experts early in neurorehabilitation technology development. Future iterations should better capture psychological and social dimensions, allow more reflection, and include the full range of relevant stakeholders through sustained transdisciplinary engagement between researchers and the LE community.

title: Fueling Inflation Risks: An Oil Shortage Scenario
text: Fueling Inflation Risks: An Oil Shortage Scenario. Central banks routinely use alternative scenarios to assess risks to the economic outlook, but these are usually generated from linear models that are unable to speak to the likelihood of extreme outcomes. We develop a nonlinear modeling framework that turns a narrative oil market scenario into a fully probabilistic assessment of the dynamics of oil and gasoline prices, aggregate inflation, and household inflation expectations. It combines an expert-based path for a tail event, a nonparametric model of the global oil market, and nonlinear Phillips curves for the energy, food, and core components of PCE inflation. We apply it in real time to quantify energy price and inflation risks of a severe oil shortage caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, modeled as a rapid drawdown of global petroleum inventories, using only information available in February 2026. Our analysis shows that once oil reserves hit rock bottom, oil and gasoline prices rise sharply, with risks tilted to the upside. Headline PCE inflation peaks near 4.8% in late 2026, and households expect inflation to rise by about 3 percentage points. Two years out, inflation is still highly likely to exceed the Fed's 2% target.

title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Resource Allocation under Institutional Asymmetry
text: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Resource Allocation under Institutional Asymmetry. We develop a two-player knapsack game to investigate resource allocation under individual capacity constraints, competition over shared resources, and institutional asymmetry. Players select feasible subsets of resources, while their payoffs depend on competitive losses, allocation rules, and asymmetric institutional benefits and costs. We derive the aggregate welfare function and show that allocation coefficients redistribute payoffs without directly affecting total welfare, whereas institutional parameters influence welfare through their net contribution. Consequently, institutional arrangements with identical welfare effects may induce different strategic incentives and Nash equilibrium outcomes. We analyze how capacity constraints and institutional priority shape equilibrium configurations and their welfare properties. A central result concerns the distinction between the social efficiency and strategic stability of shared resources. We derive conditions under which sharing is socially preferable to exclusive allocation yet remains strategically unstable because the non-priority player can increase their payoff by abandoning the resource. Conversely, sharing may remain strategically stable even when exclusive allocation yields higher aggregate welfare. These findings demonstrate that social efficiency and strategic stability need not coincide under institutional asymmetry.

title: Learning Global Equilibria in Non-Concave Prospect Theoretic Games
text: Learning Global Equilibria in Non-Concave Prospect Theoretic Games. Human agents in non cooperative games often exhibit non rational behaviour. Prospect theory provides a behavioural framework to capture how agents perceive gains and losses under risk, but, its incorporation into games typically leads to non concave and non convex utility functions, making equilibrium computation challenging. In such cases, it is difficult to obtain algorithms that have global convergence behaviour. This paper proposes a learning algorithm which uses minorization-maximization (MM). Under a proximal Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on the potential function, we establish global convergence of the algorithm to a potential-maximizing Nash equilibrium. We further show how the structure of the MM minorizer can be used to enable a distributed implementation of the algorithm. With additional noise injection, the individual updates of the agents can be obscured, while still ensuring global convergence.

title: Beyond formula CDM: Probing Structure Growth and Observational Viability of Generalized formula Gravity
text: Beyond formula CDM: Probing Structure Growth and Observational Viability of Generalized formula Gravity. formula gravity is a well-known extension of formula gravity, obtained through non-minimal or additive minimal coupling in the action's Lagrangian density. Background-level cosmography within this framework, along with comparisons to formula CDM, has been the focus of prior studies. The present work considers a generalized power-law form of the additive minimal coupling, formula , from which the Hubble function formula is derived through a novel parametrization. When formula , the matter continuity equation is rendered non-conserved, a feature that can be interpreted as an effective particle-creation mechanism. Constraints on the model parameters are obtained from Observational Hubble Data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and three SNe Ia compilations (Pantheon+, Union3, DES-SN5YR), allowing their cosmographic effects to be examined. Beyond the background level, the perturbed field, Euler, and continuity equations are derived under non-conservation, and their impact on structure growth is studied through a joint analysis incorporating the formula probe. Bayesian evidence, computed relative to formula CDM, shows that the model is favoured by background data in several cases, with moderate support for one realisation, whereas the inclusion of formula drives formula and decisively disfavours the additional freedom, highlighting the importance of growth data in testing such extensions.

title: Opacity of Discrete Event Systems under Sensor Attacks
text: Opacity of Discrete Event Systems under Sensor Attacks. Many information control problems in discrete event systems can be addressed using strong opacity, weak opacity, and non-opacity. These opacities depend on observations. If cyber attackers can attack sensors (or observation channels), then opacities will change. An opaque system may become not opaque, or a not opaque system may become opaque. Therefore, it is important to investigate opacities under sensor attacks. In this paper, we consider opacities under sensor attacks for two settings. The first one is the user has prior knowledge of sensor attacks in which the opacities are called as W-CA-opacities. The second one is the user has no prior knowledge of sensor attacks, and opacities are called as N-CA-opacities. For the former, we construct an augmented automaton that integrates the information of sensor attacks and then converts W-CA-opacities into classical opacities to solve the verification problem. For the latter, we construct the observers for the given system without sensor attacks and with sensor attacks, respectively. We then do the parallel operation on these two observers to obtain a method of verifying N-CA opacities. Furthermore, by adopting the detector technique, we find polynomial algorithms for verifying weak opacity and non opacity for both settings.

title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
text: Kinematic Quantum Geometry. Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.

title: Decode Token Parallelism: Memory-Efficient Distributed Attention Parallelism for Scalable LLM Decoding
text: Decode Token Parallelism: Memory-Efficient Distributed Attention Parallelism for Scalable LLM Decoding. Serving large language models at high concurrency with long contexts requires KV-cache capacity and attention bandwidth that grow with the decode pool. Existing parallelization strategies trade one against the other: data parallelism replicates model weights, limiting KV capacity; tensor parallelism stops scaling attention at the model's KV-head count and pushes dense collectives across nodes; and decode context parallelism (DCP) recovers capacity by sharding the sequence but adds cross-node aggregation of partial attention results. We observe that during decode, dense layers and attention scale differently: dense layers amortize weight reads across the batch and run efficiently within a single NVLink domain, whereas attention cost grows with every active request's KV cache. We present Decode Token Parallelism (TKNP), a decode-pool architecture that decouples weight placement from attention ownership. TKNP distributes a single model copy across nodes in balanced layer blocks. The active node holding a block executes its projections and MLP for the full batch using intra-node tensor parallelism, while every node computes attention for its own requests against locally resident KV cache. This extends request-local attention across nodes without replicating weights: only current-token activations cross the network, dense all-reduces remain within NVLink, and attention requires no cross-node merging of partial results. Implemented in vLLM and evaluated on Llama 3.1 405B and Nemotron-4 340B on up to 64 H100 GPUs, TKNP improves completion throughput for long-context, high-concurrency workloads by up to 1.7 formula over DCP and by up to 2.06 formula over data parallelism at matched GPU count.

title: Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems
text: Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems. We introduce two complementary frameworks for studying local periodicity and recurrence in dynamical systems. In the topological setting, we consider continuous maps with nonempty periodic-point sets, restricted to the closures of their periodic points. We define the periodic penetration time of an open set as the least period of a periodic point it contains. Using dynamically refined finite generating covers, we construct asymptotic mean and variance invariants that describe local periodic penetration relative to the logarithms of minimum subcover cardinalities. We establish their invariance under topological conjugacy and investigate their behavior for finite periodic systems, full shifts, shifts of finite type, and zero-entropy systems with dense periodic points. We also extend the construction to invertible systems using symmetric dynamical refinements. In the measure theoretic setting, we define local return times through positive measure intersections of measurable sets with their iterated preimages. Using dynamically refined finite generating partitions, we construct corresponding asymptotic mean and variance invariants and establish their invariance under measure-theoretic isomorphism. We derive explicit formulas for finite probability-preserving systems and study finite periodic approximations of uniform Bernoulli shifts on formula symbols, proving that their system-level mean and variance invariants converge to formula and formula , respectively. Our results demonstrate that local periodic penetration and return-time statistics provide information about dynamical systems beyond that captured by classical entropy.

title: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
text: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization. Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless formula -body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare formula CDM with four PMF models, formula , formula , formula , and formula , at formula . With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by formula -- formula , with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from formula for formula CDM to formula -- formula . These simulation-relative offsets span formula -- formula times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, formula , and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency formula is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near formula and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.

title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
text: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes. We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope formula is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of formula are the vertices of a bipolar polytope formula , and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of formula and formula is a convex realization of formula whenever the normal fan and the face fan of formula satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of formula -polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.

title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
text: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance. Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
text: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars. The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a formula -law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass formula and the compactness formula . Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with formula are stable only for formula and formula , a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

title: An Eyring-Kramers Formula for Singular Wells
text: An Eyring-Kramers Formula for Singular Wells. Understanding the persistence of learned behaviors in AI safety motivates an investigation of the dynamical counterpart to the equilibrium geometry studied in singular learning theory. We analyze this persistence through transitions between singular wells. We establish an Eyring-Kramers formula for a low temperature Langevin diffusion between two compact connected zero components of a real-analytic potential. The wells may be singular and nonisolated, and the unique minimizing gate is a nondegenerate index-one saddle, with gates understood as inclusion-minimal sets meeting every minimizing path. A boundary-gate construction shows that uniqueness of this inclusion-minimal gate is equivalent to every minimizing path passing through the saddle and one such path meeting the communication level only there. Compact semianalytic topology provides a separating function away from a fixed saddle neighborhood; analytic Morse coordinates give matching capacity bounds by first sending the temperature to zero and then shrinking that neighborhood. An anchored energy estimate and a small-ball potential-theoretic identity give uniformity for deterministic starting points. The leading constant is expressed in terms of the sublevel-volume coefficient, a Gamma factor, and the saddle Hessian.

title: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
text: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries. It is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. We show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. Using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

title: Galop: Billion-Scale Genetic Programming on a Single GPU
text: Galop: Billion-Scale Genetic Programming on a Single GPU. Genetic programming (GP) evolves populations of heterogeneous programs, whereas GPUs achieve their highest throughput when groups of threads execute the same instructions. To better align GP evaluation with GPU execution, we present Galop, a hybrid CPU-GPU linear GP system that assigns one individual to each CUDA warp, a group of 32 threads that execute the same instructions across different fitness cases. We compare Galop against EvoGP, a recent high-performance GPU-based tree GP system, on data-rich symbolic regression across two unique GPUs, varying population size and fitness-case count. Galop completes evolutionary runs faster than EvoGP in 27 of the 28 main comparisons, with speedups of up to 13.6 times. Solution quality comparisons favour EvoGP overall, although Galop remains competitive on several problems. Galop also completes a full generation with 2.15 billion individuals on a single H100 GPU, approximately 4.0 times the largest population achieved by any other tested GP system. All five runs at this population complete 100 generations, with a median wall-clock time of 2.23 hours. These results make it practical to study GP populations in the billions on a single GPU. Galop's source code, experimental data, and reproducibility scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/xavierhillroy/Galop.

title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
text: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy. We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

title: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning
text: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning. Quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) has emerged as a promising approach for controlling quantum systems and accelerating learning tasks with quantum resources. However, most existing QRL formulations still retain a classical reinforcement learning interface: states and actions are often encoded in computational bases and rewards are extracted through measurements. This interface is restrictive for genuinely quantum environments: choosing a measurement can discard entanglement information, while repeated intermediate measurements collapse the evolving state and require costly re-preparation. This motivates a fully QRL framework in which the agent, environment, rewards, and return accumulation are all quantum. In this paper, we take a step toward this goal and introduce a new QRL framework in which both the policy and the environment are modeled by conditional quantum channels. We then propose a quantum policy-gradient algorithm for parameterized conditional quantum channels with a trainable control basis. We also derive finite- and infinite-horizon gradient estimators using a new parameter-shift rule. This rule is needed because policy parameters are shared across repeated interaction blocks and the infinite-horizon objective is not a finite circuit; rather than shifting every occurrence and evaluating the whole trajectory, our estimator shifts only one sampled policy block. Sampling this block from a geometric distribution yields an unbiased gradient estimator under bounded rewards. Finally, we establish convergence of the resulting stochastic gradient-ascent procedure to stationary points under standard smoothness and step-size assumptions.

title: Quantum Computing in Power Systems:Current Landscape and Future Roadmap with AI
text: Quantum Computing in Power Systems:Current Landscape and Future Roadmap with AI. Modern power systems are characterized by greater penetration of renewable energy resources, extensive use of power electronics, and more diverse loads. This leads to a dramatic increase in computational complexity, which, in turn, compromises solution efficiency and fails to satisfy the real time demands of system analysis. Recently, quantum computing techniques, attributed to their unique physical properties, such as superposition and entanglement, hold the potential to offer new solutions for power systems. To this end, this paper not only provides a comprehensive landscape of quantum computing in power systems, but also investigates its roadmap with AI enabled evolution. This paper begins with an introduction to the fundamental concepts of quantum computing, followed by a review of several approaches to power system simulation and optimization. Subsequently, we further investigate the potential quantum AI-enabled evolution in power systems. In addition, the current development of quantum software and hardware platforms is elaborated. Finally, this paper synthesizes the prevailing challenges and prospects for future research directions.

title: Structural Analysis of Object-Valued Time Series
text: Structural Analysis of Object-Valued Time Series. We develop inference for structural patterns in the temporal association of object-valued time series. Our framework is built on pairwise lag profiles, which record the expected value of a chosen pairwise function at each lag and serve as a unified inferential target. We consider three representative structural features: whether a profile reaches stability beyond a finite lag, remains constant over time, and displays geometric regularity at short lags. To assess these properties, we design statistical tests calibrated by a common block multiplier bootstrap that accommodates serial dependence and the overlap inherent in lagged pairs. Gaussian approximation results establish bootstrap validity for asymptotic size control, while suitable signal conditions guarantee consistency against the corresponding alternatives. Finite-sample performance is examined through simulations in both Euclidean and density-valued settings. Applications to electricity load curves and stock-return distributions illustrate how the proposed procedures characterize association across lags.

title: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy
text: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has shifted the alignment paradigm of large language models from subjective preference to objective correctness, yet a fundamental disconnect persists between exploration diversity and reasoning validity. Existing strategies predominantly rely on "blind" entropy metrics, e.g., token-level or global sequence-level entropy, which structurally fail to distinguish between effective reasoning and potential hallucinations. This misalignment creates an illusion of diversity, where high entropy tends to signal chaotic degeneration rather than valuable exploration. To bridge this gap, we introduce Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy concept that quantifies diversity exclusively within the valid subspace and systematically filters out the noise of incorrect trajectories. Built on this concept, we instantiate VEPO, a simple Validity-aware Entropy Policy Optimization method that directly incorporates effective entropy into RLVR training. VEPO induces an adaptive attraction dynamic that drives up the probability of under-explored valid trajectories, a mechanism that matches the practical regime of large-scale autoregressive models where sequence probabilities remain extremely small. Experiments on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks with 1.5B and 7B DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models show consistent aggregate accuracy gains over GRPO and competitive repeated-sampling success. A direct evaluation with matched correct counts finds more distinct strategies on commonly solved MATH500 problems, supported by paired statistical tests and three-seed training comparisons.

title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement
text: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement. Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits. Two benchmarking findings explain why this went unnoticed. The standard CIRCLE-seq file lists ten guides under eighty on-target strings, so grouping cross-validation on the sequence column trains and tests on one guide; corrected, pair-level discrimination and per-guide fidelity collapse. With that leakage removed, a training-free position-weight score and a bare count of near-match genomic sites are not beaten by a trained oracle. We give the corrected protocol, the baselines a new model must beat, and the cohort size a certified pipeline needs.

title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
text: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation. We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index formula . Through the Plebanski correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium formula and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies formula at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling formula , with coefficients independently validated for formula . The transmission cross section tends to formula , while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

title: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks
text: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks. Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.

title: Polarized gluon TMD fragmentation into spin-1 quarkonium at NLO
text: Polarized gluon TMD fragmentation into spin-1 quarkonium at NLO. We compute the complete set of gluon transverse-momentum-dependent fragmentation functions (TMDFFs) into quarkonium through next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD. We account for all polarization configurations of both the fragmenting gluon and the produced formula quarkonium. Within NRQCD, we include all color-octet channels that contribute through formula at the considered order in the heavy-quark relative velocity formula , namely formula , formula and formula . Several structures of the calculation follow only from the spin-1 nature of the final-state hadron, so our framework applies more generally to the fragmentation of a gluon into any spin-1 hadron. Our results agree with all known collinear fragmentation functions, up to differences in formula terms that we discuss, and with the TMDFFs at LO, and we cross-check the unpolarized TMDFFs at NLO against previous calculations. Most of the polarized TMDFFs, and their full transverse-momentum dependence, are presented here for the first time. They provide the perturbative input for studies of quarkonium polarization in jets, at the EIC and in formula annihilation.

title: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime
text: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime. We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when formula , where formula denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob formula -transform with explicit function formula . We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on formula and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all formula .

title: FuGIBench: Evaluating Reliable Preparation in Streaming Video
text: FuGIBench: Evaluating Reliable Preparation in Streaming Video. An assistant watching a worker can prepare for an emerging need before the worker is ready to receive help.As the need evolves, the assistant must maintain preparation until a response is due, or withdraw it if the need disappears. Video anticipation and interactive response benchmarks leave this interval between early evidence and response largely unmeasured. We introduce FuGIBench (Future-Grounded Interaction), a streaming-video benchmark in which a model chooses among waiting, reversible preparation, and response given a causal video prefix and a task contract. The benchmark contains 19,893 synthetic tool-assistance videos across ten tool tasks, in handover, ordinary-activity, and cancelled-need tracks. One primary score credits sustained preparation, incorporates response-interval alignment, and penalizes activity when the reference prescribes waiting. On a frozen set of 1,000 episodes, a reference system with a longer preparation lead has poorer response alignment, while similar handover leads accompany different levels of activity during ordinary work in matched scenarios. Together with cancellation analyses, these results show why evaluating preparation requires tracking decisions as needs develop, become actionable, or disappear.

title: The q-Jack Lemma and Its Applications
text: The q-Jack Lemma and Its Applications. In this paper, we establish a Jackson formula -difference analogue of Jack's lemma and its higher-order extension by Miller and Mocanu, which serve as cornerstone tools in geometric function theory and differential subordination. Applying this foundation, we establish formula -counterparts of Nunokawa's boundary theorem and the Miller-Mocanu subordination lemma, and deduce applications to circular enclosure bounds. All obtained results naturally recover their classical counterparts in the limiting case as formula .

title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
text: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements. We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle.
